articles.title: I Want To Play The Villain makes keeping bratty actors happy a surprisingly enjoyable endeavour
articles.summary: In media, I generally prefer the villain. Because they don't have to worry about boring things like morals, they're often far more interesting than their goodie-goodie counterparts. So, when I heard the name I Want to Play the Villain, I figured I'd finally get to live out my dreams as some malevolent entity. Imagine my disappointment, then, when I found out it's effectively a team management simulator where the goal is to keep actors happy. That disappointment quickly evaporated, though. I love a puzzler that takes a simple concept, then slowly adds layers of complexity, constantly offering up new challenges without spiking the difficulty out of nowhere. Here, that's matching actors with roles, taking into account their various, sometimes bratty demands. The key to theatre success, evidently, is bowing to everyone's needs. ... [ MORE ]
